subject: SLA treatment for batched inference workloads / smoothing & remedy proposal
messages:
From: Miriam Cole <miriam@quantedge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@quantedge.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA for batched inference workloads — monthly credits question

Hi Jordan / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. QuantEdge is excited about using Redwood for our batched scoring pipelines (large nightly jobs + some interactive fallbacks). Before we move to a pilot, our procurement and ops teams flagged two items in the SLA that we need clarity on:

1) Standard uptime target: your template references a 99.95% monthly uptime. For heavy-batched/periodic workloads we see bursty degradation patterns that don't map well to per-minute SLOs. Would Redwood consider a lower committed uptime for the batched tier (we were thinking 98.5% as a starting point) while still providing a proportional remedy?

2) Monthly remedy mechanics: we often run large monthly jobs and would prefer a smoothing mechanism (carryover credits, or a buffer pool) rather than seeing a full invoice hit in the month of a scheduled multi-hour degradation. Can you share typical credit calculation examples and whether carryover is on the table?

I've attached a short overview of our batch profile (nightly windows, percent of traffic, expected token volume). Happy to jump on a quick call.

Best,
Miriam
Head of ML Ops, QuantEdge
[Attachment: quantedge-batched-inference-overview.pdf (pdf, 90 KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Miriam Cole <miriam@quantedge.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@quantedge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Dec 2025 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA for batched inference workloads — monthly credits question

Miriam — thanks for the clear note and the profile. This is a common tension for customers mixing interactive and batched inference. Two quick points and a proposed path forward:

- Lower committed uptime: we can pilot a dedicated "batched tier" with a 99.0% or 98.5% baseline for a limited period (90-day pilot). The tradeoff is a modest increase in the per-token price for that tier to account for lower engineering guarantees; we can surface numbers in the next message.

- Smoothing & buffer pool: we can add a "Smoothing Annex" to the SLA that allows up to 2x carryover of monthly remedy credits into the following month (cap: 50% of monthly invoice), and an optional pooled buffer of credits that absorbs one large event per quarter without immediate invoice impact. The buffer would be replenished from subsequent months.

If that sounds reasonable, I'll loop in Ben (pricing/legal) and Laura (contracts) to draft a short amendment and a worked example of the credit math. Proposed next step: Draft amendment + worked example attached, then a 30-minute call to align.

Jordan Blake
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Miriam / Samir — copying Jordan and Laura. Quick legal/finance framing on the proposed smoothing language:

1) Credit formula suggestion (to keep it simple and predictable):
- Monthly remedy = min((Downtime_minutes / Total_minutes_in_month) * Monthly_recurring_fee, Monthly_recurring_fee_cap)
- Recommended cap = 100% of monthly invoice for any single month (standard practice).

2) Carryover & buffer:
- We can allow carryover of unused remedy credits to the next calendar month up to 50% of that month’s invoice; any leftover credits expire after month+1.
- Buffer pool: one non-cumulative buffer event per quarter (up to X hours) that does not trigger immediate remediation; subsequent months reconcile.

3) Maintenance carveouts & telemetry: we require scheduled maintenance windows to be excluded (standard), and ask that QuantEdge provide the batched job schedule to help classify incidents vs. known load patterns. For operational transparency we will expose a per-route latency & availability dashboard; defined degradation events for batched workloads will be tied to the same telemetry.

If QuantEdge is comfortable with the cap and the 90-day pilot, legal can produce a redline. Attaching an initial redline for your review.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Ops & Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Miriam / Samir — thanks, all. Quick summary and agreed next steps so we have the same expectations: 

1) Pilot: 90-day pilot on a "batched inference" tier with a 99.0% uptime baseline (quantitative: monthly uptime measured at route-level, with batched routes identified).

2) Remedy mechanics: use Ben's proposed formula with a cap at 100% of monthly invoice. We will include: 2x carryover of remedy credits into the following month (carryover cap = 50% of that next month's invoice); unused carryover expires after one month.

3) Buffer pool: allow one buffered event per quarter (technical cap: up to 8 hours) that is remediated via the buffer rather than immediate invoice credit; buffer replenished from future months.

4) Maintenance & telemetry: we will exclude scheduled maintenance (48-hour notice recommended) and expect QuantEdge to share nightly job schedule (cron windows) to help classify incidents. We'll provide a per-route availability dashboard as evidence for any remediation.

5) Docs & signature: Ben's redline + Jordan's proposed amendment are attached. If QuantEdge agrees, we'll schedule a 30-minute legal/ops call this week and prepare an amendment for signature (DocuSign) by end of the month.

Please confirm by reply and indicate two time slots that work for you.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot started.
